title: Knowledge check: Working with Different Database Systems

questions.prompt: For “Working with Different Database Systems”, which approach best supports a reliable result?
options: Inspect assumptions, run a small example, and verify an edge case.
Trust the first output without inspecting its inputs.
Hide warnings and skip validation to make the result look clean.
Change several unrelated parts at once so the cause of any result is unclear.
questions.answer_key: Inspect assumptions, run a small example, and verify an edge case.
questions.explanation: External integrations fail in ordinary ways: invalid inputs, credentials, timeouts, status errors and schema changes must be handled explicitly. Reliable work makes assumptions visible and checks behavior before scaling up.

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under “Working with Different Database Systems” in the source curriculum?
options: Change unrelated settings before checking the input
Assume one example proves every edge case
Skip validation when the output looks plausible
questions.explanation: The source PDF lists “SQLite with RSQLite” as part of lesson 169. The lesson retains the original topic wording.

questions.prompt: When applying “Working with Different Database Systems” to real work, what should you do before relying on the result?
options: Validate inputs and output shape, test a boundary case, and state limitations.
Assume missing and malformed inputs never occur.
Use the same method regardless of data type or the research question.
Remove inconvenient observations without recording the decision.
questions.answer_key: Validate inputs and output shape, test a boundary case, and state limitations.
questions.explanation: Sketch a least-privilege workflow with input validation, timeout/status checks and resource cleanup; do not use production credentials. Record assumptions and known limitations instead of presenting a demonstration as proof.
